text:
This that irks--
Thy sense-life, thrilling to the elements--
Bringing thee heat and cold, sorrows and joys,
'Tis brief and mutable! Bear with it, Prince!
As the wise bear. The soul which is not moved,
The soul that with a strong and constant calm
Takes sorrow and takes joy indifferently,
Lives in the life undying!
note: Bearing passing pain and joy with steady calm

tags.when_helps: Someone tossed between highs and lows who needs reminding that passing sensations can be borne calmly.

text:
Nay, but as when one layeth
His worn-out robes away,
And taking new ones, sayeth,
"These will I wear to-day!"
So putteth by the spirit
Lightly its garb of flesh,
And passeth to inherit
A residence afresh.
note: Death as changing worn-out clothes; comfort in loss

tags.when_helps: Someone mourning a death who is open to seeing the body as a garment the spirit sets aside.

text:
The birth
Of living things comes unperceived; the death
Comes unperceived; between them, beings perceive:
What is there sorrowful herein, dear Prince?
note: Mourning; life and death as natural passage

tags.when_helps: A mourner ready to reflect on how birth and death lie beyond our sight, and to question the weight of sorrow.

text:
But thou, want not! ask not! Find full reward
Of doing right in right! Let right deeds be
Thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.
And live in action! Labour! Make thine acts
Thy piety, casting all self aside,
Contemning gain and merit; equable
In good or evil: equability
Is Yog, is piety!
note: Work without craving results; doing right for its own sake

tags.when_helps: Someone fixated on results or rewards at work who needs to focus on doing the right thing for its own sake.

Yet, the right act
Is less, far less, than the right-thinking mind.
Seek refuge in thy soul; have there thy heaven!
Scorn them that follow virtue for her gifts!
note: Inner refuge; goodness without seeking reward

tags.when_helps: A person doing good outwardly but uneasy inside, ready to look at the motives and mind behind their actions.

text:
In sorrows not dejected, and in joys
Not overjoyed; dwelling outside the stress
Of passion, fear, and anger; fixed in calms
Of lofty contemplation;--such an one
Is Muni, is the Sage, the true Recluse!
note: Steadiness through sorrow, joy, fear and anger

tags.when_helps: Someone swept up by fear or anger who wants a picture of the calm, steady person they hope to become.

text:
If one
Ponders on objects of the sense, there springs
Attraction; from attraction grows desire,
Desire flames to fierce passion, passion breeds
Recklessness; then the memory--all betrayed--
Lets noble purpose go, and saps the mind,
Till purpose, mind, and man are all undone.
But, if one deals with objects of the sense
Not loving and not hating, making them
Serve his free soul, which rests serenely lord,
Lo! such a man comes to tranquillity;
And out of that tranquillity shall rise
The end and healing of his earthly pains,
Since the will governed sets the soul at peace.
note: How craving spirals; self-mastery brings peace

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone caught in a spiral of wanting who needs to see how desire grows from attention and how to step out of it.

text:
And like the ocean, day by day receiving
Floods from all lands, which never overflows
Its boundary-line not leaping, and not leaving,
Fed by the rivers, but unswelled by those;--
So is the perfect one! to his soul's ocean
The world of sense pours streams of witchery;
They leave him as they find, without commotion,
Taking their tribute, but remaining sea.
note: Staying calm and whole amid constant temptation

tags.when_helps: A person flooded by stimulation and temptation who wants an image of staying whole and unmoved.

text:
Finally, this is better, that one do
His own task as he may, even though he fail,
Than take tasks not his own, though they seem good.
To die performing duty is no ill;
But who seeks other roads shall wander still.
note: Following your own path rather than envying others'

situations: a career change or new job
tags.safety_reason: Read alone, the line that dying in one's duty is no ill frames death as acceptable, so it should not reach a reader in distress.
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to chase another's path who needs encouragement to do their own work, even imperfectly.

text:
Moreover, Son of Pandu! wert thou worst
Of all wrong-doers, this fair ship of Truth
Should bear thee safe and dry across the sea
Of thy transgressions.
note: Guilt over past wrongs; truth can still carry you

text:
Be not over-glad
Attaining joy, and be not over-sad
Encountering grief, but, stayed on Brahma, still
Constant let each abide!
note: Staying steady through highs and lows

tags.when_helps: A believer swinging between elation and sadness who wants to stay anchored in the divine.

text:
The joys
Springing from sense-life are but quickening wombs
Which breed sure griefs: those joys begin and end!
The wise mind takes no pleasure, Kunti's Son!
In such as those! But if a man shall learn,
Even while he lives and bears his body's chain,
To master lust and anger, he is blest!
note: Fleeting pleasures; mastering craving and anger

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone chasing pleasures that keep ending in pain, ready to work on mastering desire and anger.

text:
But for earthly needs
Religion is not his who too much fasts
Or too much feasts, nor his who sleeps away
An idle mind; nor his who wears to waste
His strength in vigils. Nay, Arjuna! call
That the true piety which most removes
Earth-aches and ills, where one is moderate
In eating and in resting, and in sport;
Measured in wish and act; sleeping betimes,
Waking betimes for duty.
note: Balance and moderation; avoiding burnout and excess

tags.when_helps: Someone pushing too hard or neglecting rest who needs a reminder that balance in eating, sleeping and effort is the real discipline.

text:
But, as often as the heart
Breaks--wild and wavering--from control, so oft
Let him re-curb it, let him rein it back
To the soul's governance; for perfect bliss
Grows only in the bosom tranquillised,
The spirit passionless, purged from offence,
Vowed to the Infinite.
note: Wandering mind in meditation; gently returning again

tags.when_helps: Someone whose attention or resolve keeps slipping, reminding them to gently bring it back each time.

Hero long-armed! beyond denial, hard
Man's heart is to restrain, and wavering;
Yet may it grow restrained by habit, Prince!
By wont of self-command.

text:
I am the fresh taste of the water; I
The silver of the moon, the gold o' the sun,
The word of worship in the Veds, the thrill
That passeth in the ether, and the strength
Of man's shed seed. I am the good sweet smell
Of the moistened earth, I am the fire's red light,
The vital air moving in all which moves,
The holiness of hallowed souls, the root
Undying, whence hath sprung whatever is;
The wisdom of the wise, the intellect
Of the informed, the greatness of the great.
note: Finding the sacred in ordinary things around us

tags.when_helps: A believer who wants to see the divine in ordinary things like water, moonlight and the smell of earth.

Whoso shall offer Me in faith and love
A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water poured forth,
That offering I accept, lovingly made
With pious will.

If one of evil life turn in his thought
Straightly to Me, count him amidst the good;
He hath the high way chosen; he shall grow
Righteous ere long; he shall attain that peace
Which changes not.

Whate'er befalls, and mirth, and tears, and piety, and thrift,

text:
Only by fullest service, perfect faith,
And uttermost surrender am I known
And seen, and entered into, Indian Prince!
Who doeth all for Me; who findeth Me
In all; adoreth always; loveth all
Which I have made, and Me, for Love's sole end
That man, Arjuna! unto Me doth wend.
note: surrender and love as the spiritual path

tags.when_helps: A devotee longing to know God, drawn to a path of full service, love and surrender.

text:
But if thy thought
Droops from such height; if thou be'st weak to set
Body and soul upon Me constantly,
Despair not! give Me lower service! seek
To reach Me, worshipping with steadfast will;
And, if thou canst not worship steadfastly,
Work for Me, toil in works pleasing to Me!
For he that laboureth right for love of Me
Shall finally attain! But, if in this
Thy faint heart fails, bring Me thy failure! find
Refuge in Me! let fruits of labour go,
Renouncing hope for Me, with lowliest heart,
So shalt thou come; for, though to know is more
Than diligence, yet worship better is
Than knowing, and renouncing better still.
Near to renunciation--very near--
Dwelleth Eternal Peace!
note: feeling weak or failing on the path; do not despair

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels too weak for their practice, reassured that even their failure can be offered and still lead to peace.

text:
Who troubleth not his kind,
And is not troubled by them; clear of wrath,
Living too high for gladness, grief, or fear,
That man I love! Who, dwelling quiet-eyed,
Stainless, serene, well-balanced, unperplexed,
Working with Me, yet from all works detached,
That man I love!
note: serenity, freedom from anger and fear

tags.when_helps: A believer stirred up by others who wants a portrait of the serene, balanced person God loves.

text:
Who, unto friend and foe
Keeping an equal heart, with equal mind
Bears shame and glory; with an equal peace
Takes heat and cold, pleasure and pain; abides
Quit of desires, hears praise or calumny
In passionless restraint, unmoved by each;
Linked by no ties to earth, steadfast in Me,
That man I love!
note: equanimity amid praise, blame, pleasure and pain

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone stung by blame or flattery who wants to keep an equal heart toward friend and foe alike.

text:
Fearlessness, singleness of soul, the will
Always to strive for wisdom; opened hand
And governed appetites; and piety,
And love of lonely study; humbleness,
Uprightness, heed to injure nought which lives,
Truthfulness, slowness unto wrath, a mind
That lightly letteth go what others prize;
And equanimity, and charity
Which spieth no man's faults; and tenderness
Towards all that suffer; a contented heart,
Fluttered by no desires; a bearing mild,
Modest, and grave, with manhood nobly mixed,
With patience, fortitude, and purity;
An unrevengeful spirit, never given
To rate itself too high;--such be the signs,
O Indian Prince! of him whose feet are set
On that fair path which leads to heavenly birth!
note: the qualities of a good life: humility, patience, kindness

tags.when_helps: Someone asking what kind of person to become, looking for a clear list of qualities to cultivate.

The Doors of Hell
Are threefold, whereby men to ruin pass,--
The door of Lust, the door of Wrath, the door
Of Avarice. Let a man shun those three!

text:
Words causing no man woe, words ever true,
Gentle and pleasing words, and those ye say
In murmured reading of a Sacred Writ,--
These make the true religiousness of Speech.

text:
But, Arjun!
Abstaining from attachment to the work,
Abstaining from rewardment in the work,
While yet one doeth it full faithfully,
Saying, "Tis right to do!" that is "true " act
And abstinence! Who doeth duties so,
Unvexed if his work fail, if it succeed
Unflattered, in his own heart justified,
Quit of debates and doubts, his is "true" act:
For, being in the body, none may stand
Wholly aloof from act; yet, who abstains
From profit of his acts is abstinent.
note: doing work well without clinging to success or failure

tags.when_helps: Someone anxious about whether their work will succeed, encouraged to do it faithfully and let go of the outcome.

Sweet as the taste of Amrit. Drink of that!

text:
Better thine own work is, though done with fault,
Than doing others' work, ev'n excellently.
He shall not fall in sin who fronts the task
Set him by Nature's hand! Let no man leave
His natural duty, Prince! though it bear blame!
For every work hath blame, as every flame
Is wrapped in smoke! Only that man attains
Perfect surcease of work whose work was wrought
With mind unfettered, soul wholly subdued,
Desires for ever dead, results renounced.
note: following your own path, imperfect work, comparison with others

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone doubting their own imperfect path who needs to hear that every work has flaws and their own duty is still better.

Listen! I tell thee for thy comfort this.
Give Me thy heart! adore Me! serve Me! cling
In faith and love and reverence to Me!
So shalt thou come to Me! I promise true,
For thou art sweet to Me!

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling unloved or far from God who needs to hear they are precious and beloved.
